prompt.brief: Design an enterprise RAG platform that ingests permissioned documents, retrieves fresh evidence, maintains conversation context, and generates cited answers with safe model fallbacks.
successSignals: Separate source documents, chunk and embedding versions, access-control metadata, conversations, prompts, and model outputs.
Use hybrid dense and sparse retrieval with reranking, bounded context, citations, and tenant-aware filters.
Make indexing asynchronous and versioned so deletes and permission changes cannot leak stale evidence.
Explain prompt injection, hallucination, model failure, feedback evaluation, cost budgets, and auditability.

functional: Upload and parse enterprise documents, chunk and embed them, and publish a searchable version with freshness status.
Answer a question with authorized retrieved passages, citations, conversation context, safety checks, and streamed output.
Support document deletion, permission changes, reindexing, feedback, evaluation sets, usage controls, and tenant export.
nonFunctional: Target p95 time to first token below 500 ms and completed grounded responses below 3 seconds for normal queries.
Scale document indexing and query traffic independently, with per-tenant quotas and bounded retrieval work.
Never lose a source document or feedback event; make embedding, indexing, generation, and tool retries safe.
Fall back to keyword search, a smaller model, or an explicit no-answer response when dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Support 10,000 queries per second, 100 million indexed chunks, and thousands of enterprise tenants.
Partition by tenant and knowledge collection; isolate large reindex jobs and hot assistants.
Retain encrypted source and audit data while keeping vector indexes, conversation context, and caches bounded.

dataFlow.title: Ingest permissioned enterprise documents
dataFlow.description: The ingestion service validates source ownership, ACLs, version, and deletion policy, then stores the canonical document before creating chunk and embedding work.

dataFlow.title: Retrieve evidence for a question
dataFlow.description: The retriever applies tenant and document ACLs, combines lexical and vector search, reranks bounded candidates, and records the index generation used.

dataFlow.title: Build a grounded conversation context
dataFlow.description: The context builder loads the conversation window, trims or summarizes within a token budget, attaches citations, and rejects evidence that is stale or unauthorized.

dataFlow.title: Generate and validate a cited answer
dataFlow.description: The model gateway uses a pinned prompt and model policy, checks citation coverage and unsafe output, and falls back to a retrieval-only response when generation is unavailable.

dataFlow.title: Stream the answer and retain the turn
dataFlow.description: The response gateway streams tokens with a resume cursor, then commits the conversation turn, citations, model version, and feedback without blocking retrieval workers.

architecture.title: Design a conversational AI platform that uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to answer questions from enterprise knowledge bases, maintains conversation context, and provides cited responses. reference architecture
architecture.summary: The ingestion path durably versions documents and asynchronously builds ACL-aware lexical and vector indexes. The query path synchronously enforces authorization, retrieves and reranks evidence, constructs a bounded context, applies safety policy, and routes generation through a model gateway before streaming cited output.

deepDives.title: ACL-aware retrieval and deletion
points: For the enterprise RAG platform, every citation must resolve to an authorized retrieved passage from a versioned source.
Design for the failure case where stale permissions, missing evidence, or a model timeout must produce a safe qualified response; keep retries, versions, and repair state explicit.
Expose freshness, version, lineage, or audit metadata so operators and clients can distinguish current, pending, and degraded state.

Keep this concern off unrelated request paths and partition it by the the enterprise RAG platform access key.

tradeoffs.title: Hybrid retrieval versus one index
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use lexical and vector retrieval with ACL filters and a lexical fallback for exact identifiers and predictable latency.
tradeoffs.caution: A vector-only design can lose exact matches and makes freshness and authorization harder to reason about.

tradeoffs.title: Long context versus bounded cost
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use a bounded conversation window, evidence budget, and deterministic summarization before generation.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded history increases token cost, latency, and the chance of unsupported claims.

tradeoffs.title: Model quality versus safe fallback
tradeoffs.recommendation: Gate generation on citation and safety checks and fall back to cited retrieval results or abstention.
tradeoffs.caution: Returning a fluent answer without evidence is worse than a transparent refusal for enterprise knowledge.

commonMistakes: Retrieving documents without applying the current ACL.
Treating vector similarity as evidence without citation coverage.
Allowing conversation context or token use to grow without bounds.
Persisting an answer without model, retrieval, and source versions.
Retrying streamed generation without a resume cursor or deduplication.

followUps.question: What happens when a document is deleted?
followUps.answer: Write a durable tombstone, invalidate chunks and caches, rebuild affected index generations, and verify old citations no longer resolve.

followUps.question: How do you prevent prompt injection from a document?
followUps.answer: Classify untrusted content, keep system policy outside retrieved text, constrain tools, and require citation and output safety checks.

followUps.question: How do you support a provider outage?
followUps.answer: Use retrieval-only or cached cited responses, apply provider circuit breakers and token budgets, and preserve the turn as pending when generation is unknown.

rubric.description: The answer defines permissioned ingestion, hybrid retrieval, citation grounding, bounded context, safe fallback, streaming, and auditability, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure behavior.
Entities and keys make the enterprise RAG platform state, versions, lifecycle, and derived projections explicit.
Partitioning, queues, backpressure, cache behavior, hot-key handling, and bounded work are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded behavior, observability, and auditability protect the primary contract.
The candidate can explain the the enterprise RAG platform consistency boundary, asynchronous work, and operational limits.
